# Server JS (`@server/next`)

> HTTP server for Node, Bun, Cloudflare Workers and Netlify. One default
> export, a chainable router, and a `ctx` object. Handlers return values, not
> `res.send()`. Full docs: https://server-js.com/documentation

## Entry

```js
import server from "@server/next";

export default server(options)
  .get('/', (ctx) => 'hello')
  .post('/users', (ctx) => db.users.create(ctx.body));
```

The default export is the `Server` itself, a [Fetchable](https://fetchable.org/)
object: runtimes read `fetch(request)` off it. Node runs the file with
`node index.js`, Bun with `bun index.js`; Cloudflare Workers and Netlify
Functions import it as their handler. Netlify Edge Functions are not supported
(they require a plain function and have no top-level await).
https://server-js.com/documentation#platforms

## Package exports

| Export | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | `(options?: Options) => Server` | Default export. Creates the server |
| `router` | `() => Router` | Standalone route chain, merged with `.use()`. https://server-js.com/documentation/router#router |
| `ServerError` | class | `new ServerError(code, status, message)`. For codes you reuse, register them once with `ServerError.extend({})`, then throw `ServerError.<CODE>(vars)`. https://server-js.com/documentation/errors#throwing-your-own |
| `ValidationError` | class | Thrown by a failing route schema; has `source` and `issues` |
| `bucket` | object | Re-export of [`bucket`](https://bucketjs.com): `bucket.FS()`, `.S3()`, `.R2()`, `.GCS()`, `.Azure()`, `.B2()`, `.Memory()` |
| `status` `headers` `type` `cache` `download` `cookies` `send` `json` `file` `redirect` | functions | Reply helpers, chainable. https://server-js.com/documentation/reply |

Types are exported too: `Context`, `Options`, `RouteOptions`, `Settings`,
`Middleware`, `UploadOptions`, `UploadedFile`, `UploadValidate`, `Bucket`,
`BucketFile`, `SecurityOptions`, `CorsOptions`, `CacheOption`, `Parser`,
`LogLevel`, `AuthMeta`, `AuthOption`.

## Server methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `.test()` | In-memory client, no port. https://server-js.com/documentation/testing |
| `.fetch(request, env?)` | The Fetchable entry point (Bun, Cloudflare Workers) |

Plus every router method below.

## Router

`.get()` `.head()` `.post()` `.put()` `.patch()` `.delete()` `.options()`
`.socket()` `.use()`, each returning the server for chaining.
https://server-js.com/documentation/router

```
.get(path?, options?, ...middleware)
.use(...middleware)
.use(router)
```

`path` is optional (same as `'*'`). Four shapes: exact (`/info`), named
parameter (`/posts/:id`), typed parameter (`/posts/:id(number)`, cast to
`number` or `Date`; an uncastable value is a `400 INVALID_PARAM` on the matched
route), wildcard (`/files/*`). Matching is exact, so `/info` never matches
`/info/extra`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/router#path

`options` is a per-route object that overrides the root ones for this route:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `body` `query` `params` `response` | `StandardSchema` | Zod, Valibot, ArkType. Validated before the route's own middleware. https://server-js.com/documentation/router#validation |
| `parser` | `'auto' \| 'raw' \| 'stream'` | Overrides the root `parser` |
| `uploads` | `path \| Bucket \| object \| false` | Replaces the root `uploads` wholesale |
| `cache` | `string \| number \| false` | `Cache-Control` for this route |
| `schema` | `object \| false` | OpenAPI metadata (tags, summary); `false` hides the route |

https://server-js.com/documentation/router#options

## Options

`server(options)`. `PORT`, `SECRETS`, `PUBLIC`, `CORS`, `AUTH` and `LOG_LEVEL`
are read from the environment when the option is not passed; an explicit option
always wins. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#environment-variables

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port` | `number` | `3000` (`PORT`) | https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsport |
| `secrets` | `string \| string[]` | random | Signs credentials; the first signs, all verify. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionssecrets |
| `public` | `string \| Bucket` | off | Folder or bucket served as static assets, before routes. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionspublic |
| `uploads` | `string \| Bucket \| UploadOptions \| false` | off | Where uploaded files are stored. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsuploads |
| `auth` | `string \| function \| object` | off (`AUTH`) | Resolves `ctx.user`; mounts login routes when it owns the flow. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsauth |
| `cors` | `boolean \| string \| string[] \| object` | off | `{ origin, methods, headers, credentials }`; `credentials: true` needs exact origins, never `*`. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionscors |
| `parser` | `'auto' \| 'raw' \| 'stream'` | `'auto'` | How bodies are read into `ctx.body`. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsparser |
| `cache` | `string \| number \| false` | off | Default `Cache-Control`. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionscache |
| `security` | `boolean \| SecurityOptions` | on | https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionssecurity |
| `openapi` | `boolean \| string \| object` | off | Serves the generated spec at `/openapi.json`. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsopenapi |
| `onError` | `(error, ctx) => Response` | built-in | https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsonerror |
| `onResponse` | `(response, ctx) => Response \| void` | none | Runs on every finalized response. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsonresponse |
| `log` | `boolean \| 'info'` | off (`LOG_LEVEL`) | Startup, connection and request lines. https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionslog |

### uploads

Object form: `{ bucket, maxFileSize, maxTotalSize, maxFiles, minFileSize, fileType, validate }`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionsuploads

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bucket` | `path \| Bucket` | required | Destination |
| `maxFileSize` | `number \| string` | `'10mb'` | Per file, enforced while streaming (`413`) |
| `maxTotalSize` | `number \| string` | `'100mb'` | Across one request (`413`) |
| `maxFiles` | `number` | `100` | Per request (`413`) |
| `minFileSize` | `number \| string` | none | Checked after the write, file removed (`400`) |
| `fileType` | `string[]` | none | Extensions (`.jpg`), MIME types (`image/jpeg`), bare names (`csv`), wildcards (`image/*`). Checked against the stored type (`415`) |
| `validate` | `(ctx) => unknown` | none | Runs before the body is read, with `ctx.user` resolved. `false` refuses with `403`; throw for your own error |

Stored files are named by the server: a random key plus the extension of the
type they are stored as. That type is what the bytes are when the format has a
signature, and the declared `Content-Type` otherwise. The client's filename is
kept as `ctx.body.<field>.name` and never reaches the bucket.

### security

`{ trustProxy, frameguard, noSniff, referrerPolicy, hsts, xssProtection,
traversalProtection, maxBodySize, csp, coop, corp, permissionsPolicy }`.
`maxBodySize` (default `'1mb'`) caps only buffered bytes; uploaded files stream
and follow the `uploads` limits instead. `trustProxy` (`boolean | string`,
default `true`) believes `x-forwarded-*` for `ctx.ip` and `ctx.url` only when
the peer is private or loopback, taking the last public hop of the chain; a
header name reads the IP from there instead, for a CDN in front of a proxy.
https://server-js.com/documentation/options#optionssecurity

## ctx

The single argument every handler and middleware receives.
https://server-js.com/documentation/context

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.method` | `string` | Lowercase. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxmethod |
| `ctx.url` | `URL & { params, query }` | https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxurl |
| `ctx.body` | parsed value | Object, string, `Buffer` or `ReadableStream` by mode. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxbody |
| `ctx.headers` | `Record<string, string \| string[]>` | Lowercased keys. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxheaders |
| `ctx.cookies` | `Record<string, string>` | https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxcookies |
| `ctx.ip` | `string` | https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxip |
| `ctx.user` | any | Set by `auth`, resolved before the body is read. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxuser |
| `ctx.auth` | `{ issuedAt, expiresAt, strategy, provider }` | https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxauth |
| `ctx.signal` | `AbortSignal` | Aborts when the client disconnects. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxsignal |
| `ctx.options` | `Settings` | Resolved config for this request |
| `ctx.platform` | `{ provider, runtime, production }` | https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxplatform |
| `ctx.time` | object | Server-Timing marks. https://server-js.com/documentation/context#ctxtime |
| `ctx.socket` / `ctx.sockets` | `WebSocket` | Inside `.socket()` handlers only |
| `ctx.app` | `Server` | The server itself |

An uploaded file on `ctx.body` is `{ name, path, type, size }`; a repeated
field name gives an array. https://server-js.com/documentation#file-handling

## Replies

Return a value and it is serialized: a string (always `text/plain`; use
`type('html')` for markup), an object or array (JSON), a `Buffer`, a
`ReadableStream`, a JSX element (`text/html`), a `Response`, or a bucket file
handle (streamed with its type, `404` when missing). A returned number is a
status code from 200 to 599 with an empty body (`return 201`); to send a number
as the body, `return json(42)`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#inline-replies

Helpers, all chainable, terminal ones return a `Response`:

| Helper | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `send(body?)` | terminal | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#send |
| `json(body)` | terminal | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#json |
| `file(path \| BucketFile)` | terminal | Streams it. https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#file |
| `redirect(path)` | terminal | `302` by default. https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#redirect |
| `status(code)` | chainable | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#status |
| `type(mime \| ext)` | chainable | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#type |
| `headers(obj)` | chainable | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#headers |
| `cookies(obj)` | chainable | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#cookies |
| `cache(value)` | chainable | https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#cache |
| `download(name?)` | chainable | `Content-Disposition: attachment`. Use it for untrusted uploads. https://server-js.com/documentation/reply#download |

## Errors

Throw anything and `onError` turns it into a response. `ServerError` carries a
stable `code`, a `status` and a `hint`. An error's status is used only when it
is 400-599; anything else, including a thrown `Response`, is a plain 500. An
`onResponse` that throws goes through `onError`; an `onError` that throws or
returns a non-Response falls back to the built-in handler rather than escaping.
https://server-js.com/documentation/errors

Registered codes: `NOT_FOUND`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `INVALID_PARAM`, `PATH_TRAVERSAL`,
`INVALID_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `BODY_TOO_LARGE`,
`BODY_INVALID_MULTIPART`, `UPLOAD_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`,
`UPLOAD_TOO_MANY_FILES`, `UPLOAD_TOO_SMALL`, `UPLOAD_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`UPLOAD_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN`, `AUTH_INVALID_HEADER`,
`AUTH_INVALID_STATE`, `AUTH_ISSUER_UNREACHABLE`, `AUTH_NO_CODE`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/errors#reference

## Authentication

`auth` loads the user, it never gates a route. Guard with `ctx.user` in the
handler; guard uploads with `uploads.validate`, since handlers and middleware
both run after the body has been parsed.
https://server-js.com/documentation/authentication#protecting-routes

String form is `'<strategy>:<name>'` (`'cookie:github'`, `'jwt:clerk'`).
Object form takes `{ providers, strategy, expires, onLogin, getUser,
toPublicUser, onLogout, redirect }`. A plain function `(ctx) => user` works,
as does an auth library instance. Email and password is out of scope: pass a
Better Auth instance for that.
https://server-js.com/documentation/authentication#a-library

Each provider reads `<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID` and `<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_SECRET`
(`GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_CLIENT_ID`), or takes
`{ clientId, clientSecret, scopes }` per provider. Extra settings use the same
prefix: `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `GITHUB_SCOPES`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/authentication#the-providers
https://server-js.com/documentation/authentication

## Testing

`.test()` returns a client with `get`, `head`, `post`, `put`, `patch`,
`delete`, `options`, each resolving to a real `Response`. It keeps a cookie jar
across calls (`api.cookies`, `api.clear()`), so signing in then calling a
protected route works.
https://server-js.com/documentation/testing

## Pipeline order

Per request: route match, `ctx.user`, `uploads.validate`, body parsing, the
route's schemas, then its chain (the built-in middleware, yours, the handler).
A request matching no route parses its body and falls through to the global
middleware, which is how static assets answer. On the way out: shared response
headers (CORS, security, cache and ETag), then `onResponse`. Middleware always
see a parsed `ctx.body`.
https://server-js.com/documentation/concepts
